_comment: #228 — deliberately LIMITED-scope mutation testing (StrykerJS), not full-repo:
1. `mutate` covers only src/lib/crypt.ts and src/lib/restore.ts — the
encrypt/decrypt/keygen core and the manifest path-traversal guards PR #198's
review finding was about — not the whole codebase.
2. WITHIN those two files, `// Stryker disable all` / `// Stryker restore all`
markers (see each file) further narrow actual mutant generation to just
generateKeypair/newEncrypter/newDecrypter (crypt.ts) and
isSafeComponentName/shortSourceLabel/sourceDigest (restore.ts —
shortSourceLabel was encodeSourcePath before #423 renamed/simplified it;
sourceDigest is new in #423) — the functions scripts/selftest-properties.mjs's
fast-check properties actually exercise.
Everything else in these two files (tar/pg_restore process orchestration,
the streaming pipeline helpers, passphrase prompting, signal-guard wiring)
has no fast in-process test oracle here — mutating it would only produce
'survived' noise, not a security signal, and would blow up run time (that
code is only exercised by the bash selftest*.sh suite, each a several-second
subprocess-spawning script — fine for a single run, far too slow per mutant).
3. This is a manual/weekly job (.github/workflows/mutation-test.yml), never part
of the per-PR ci.yml — the whole point of #228's 'limited' framing is to add
a continuous security tripwire without inflating everyday CI time.
4. `ignorePatterns` excludes tsconfig.json from the mutation sandbox copy on
purpose: @stryker-mutator/core@9.6.1's TSConfigPreprocessor calls the classic
`ts.parseConfigFileTextToJson` API, which this project's `typescript@^7.0.2`
(the new Go-based compiler) no longer exports, so Stryker crashes if it finds
a tsconfig.json to rewrite. The command runner below never invokes tsc — this
project runs TS straight off source via node's --experimental-strip-types (see
scripts/dev-node-flags.mjs) — so excluding it costs nothing.
5. Measured score across several local runs (PRE-#423, against the old
encodeSourcePath()): crypt.ts consistently 100%; restore.ts ~77-83% (varies a
little run to run — scripts/selftest-properties.mjs does not pin an explicit
fast-check seed, so which edge cases get sampled, and therefore which mutants
happen to get caught, shifts slightly). Every restore.ts survivor observed so
far sat inside encodeSourcePath()'s cosmetic display-name encoding — e.g. whether
a LEADING path separator was stripped before the general character-class
substitution ran, or whether an already-short input took the truncate-and-hash
branch unnecessarily. None of them let a separator or an over-length segment
through — the properties this file actually asserts. #423 replaced
encodeSourcePath() with the simpler shortSourceLabel() (no truncate-and-hash
branch left — see src/lib/restore.ts) and added a third property pinning
directory-name uniqueness; this specific survivor characterization has not been
re-measured against that new code, so treat it as historical context, not a
current number. `thresholds` below is left with the same headroom either way.
6. `concurrency: 1` is deliberate, not a default left untouched: each mutant run
spawns a fresh node process that generates a post-quantum (ML-KEM-768) keypair
a few times over (see the roundtrip property), and under Stryker's default
multi-worker concurrency this project's dev machine produced runs where CPU
contention alone pushed some mutants over the per-mutant timeout — a run that
is merely SLOW is not the same finding as a mutant a test actually caught, and
scoring them the same way (Stryker counts a timeout as 'killed') made the
reported score swing between ~83% and 100% run to run with no code change.
Sequential execution removes that source of noise; this suite is fast enough
in absolute terms (~1 minute total) that giving up worker parallelism here
costs little.
Widening either the file list or the in-file scope is reasonable future work
(e.g. wiring the bash selftests in as a slower, more complete oracle) — just do
it deliberately, matching the oracle to what actually runs per mutant.
